rows.text: Megatron is a damage cannon that fires artifacts. On the Vehicle side, every attack sacrifices an artifact and deals damage equal to its MANA VALUE to a creature — and any excess goes to that creature's controller. Sacrifice an eleven-drop, point it at a 1/1, and eleven damage hits a face. The deck is built to have enormous artifacts in the graveyard, get them onto the battlefield cheaply, and feed them to the cannon.

rows.name: Megatron, Tyrant
rows.text: cast him CONVERTED for {1}{R}{W}{B} — four mana instead of his printed cost — and he arrives as the Vehicle with living metal, so he is a creature on your turn without needing crew.

On the Tyrant side, opponents cannot cast spells during combat at all, and converting in your postcombat main adds {C} for every point of life your opponents lost this turn. A big cannon shot pays for the next fatty.

rows.name: Basilisk Collar
rows.text: this is the multiplier. Deathtouch means one damage is lethal to ANY creature, so every point past the first is excess and goes to the face. Sacrificing a mana value twelve artifact deals eleven to a player regardless of what you pointed it at.

rows.name: Isshin, Two Heavens as One
rows.text: Megatron's attack trigger is an attack trigger, so it happens twice. Two artifacts sacrificed, two bursts of damage, in one combat.

rows.name: Lightning Greaves
rows.text: haste and shroud.
Every one of these is a huge mana value, which is the only stat the cannon reads.

rows.name: Excalibur, Sword of Eden
rows.text: mana value twelve, and its cost falls by your historic permanents, so it is castable as well as loadable.

rows.name: Metalwork Colossus
rows.text: mana value eleven, nearly free to cast with noncreature artifacts out, and it returns itself from the graveyard for two artifacts.

rows.name: Mycosynth Golem
rows.text: mana value eleven, and it gives every artifact creature spell affinity so the rest of the ammunition costs almost nothing.

rows.name: Panther Robot
rows.text: mana value ten with affinity.

rows.name: Ancient Stone Idol
rows.text: mana value ten, flash, and it leaves a 6/12 behind when it dies.

rows.name: Phyrexian Triniform
rows.text: mana value nine, and it dies into three 3/3s.

rows.name: Bygone Colossus
rows.text: mana value nine, and warp lets you play it for three now and cast it properly later.

rows.name: Cityscape Leveler
rows.text: mana value eight, destroys a permanent on cast and on every attack, and unearths.

rows.name: Imskir Iron-Eater
rows.text: a second cannon — sacrifice an artifact to deal its mana value to ANY target, no creature required.

guide.title: Getting them into the graveyard and back

rows.name: Buried Alive
rows.text: three fatties straight into the yard.

rows.name: Faithless Looting
rows.text: cheap filtering, twice.

rows.name: Goblin Engineer
rows.text: tutors an artifact directly into the graveyard, then recurs cheap ones.

rows.name: Goblin Welder
rows.text: swaps an artifact you control for a better one in the graveyard, every turn, free.

rows.name: Mishra, Tamer of Mak Fawa
rows.text: every artifact card in your graveyard gains unearth {1}{B}{R}. That is three mana to put a mana-value-eleven cannon shell onto the battlefield, and it also gives your whole board a ward.

rows.name: Daretti, Rocketeer Engineer
rows.text: returns an artifact from the graveyard on entry and on every attack.

rows.name: Daretti, Scrap Savant
rows.text: rummages, reanimates an artifact on the minus, and the ultimate returns every artifact that dies from then on.

rows.name: Kuldotha Forgemaster
rows.text: three artifacts becomes any artifact in the deck, straight onto the battlefield.

rows.name: Animate Dead
rows.text: cheap reanimation for the artifact creatures.

rows.name: Necromancy
rows.text: at flash speed, so you can rebuild in response to a wrath.

rows.name: Persist
rows.text: two mana for any nonlegendary creature.

rows.name: Morbid Curiosity
rows.text: sacrifice a fatty and draw cards equal to its mana value. Eleven cards is not unusual.

rows.name: Krang, Utrom Warlord
rows.text: every other artifact creature gains flying, trample, indestructible and haste. It turns a board of ammunition into an army.

rows.name: Anger
rows.text: sitting in the graveyard with a Mountain out, everything you reanimate has haste.

rows.name: Grand Abolisher
rows.text: nobody interacts on your turn.

rows.name: Megatron, Tyrant
rows.text: the Tyrant side already stops opponents casting during combat, which covers the window that matters most.

rows.name: Boros Charm
rows.text: indestructible for the board through a wrath, or double strike, or four to the face.

rows.name: Clever Concealment
rows.text: usually free with convoke, and it phases the board out of a sweeper.

rows.name: Deflecting Swat
rows.text: free, and it redirects the removal aimed at Megatron mid-combat.

rows.name: Demonic Junker
rows.text: destroys a creature from every player at once, and grows if one of yours died.

rows.name: Organic Extinction
rows.text: improvise makes it cheap, and it destroys every NONARTIFACT creature — a one-sided wrath here.

rows.name: Cityscape Leveler
rows.text: a permanent destroyed on cast and on every attack.

rows.name: Combustible Gearhulk
rows.text: three cards, or three milled cards' worth of damage — and milling yourself loads the cannon.

rows.name: Imskir Iron-Eater
rows.text: draws off your artifact count and throws artifacts at anything.

rows.name: Mox Opal
rows.text: metalcraft is trivial here.

rows.name: Arcane Signet
rows.text: fixing three colours.

rows.name: Fellwar Stone
rows.text: usually taps for what you need.

rows.name: Mycosynth Golem
rows.text: affinity on every artifact creature spell — the single biggest cost reducer.

rows.name: Metalwork Colossus
rows.text: effectively free with a few rocks down.

rows.name: Demonic Tutor
rows.text: any card.

rows.name: Enlightened Tutor
rows.text: any artifact, to the top.

rows.name: Esper Sentinel
rows.text: taxes their first noncreature spell each turn.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep a graveyard enabler and acceleration. Buried Alive or Goblin Engineer plus a rock means Megatron converts on turn four with a mana-value-eleven shell already waiting in the yard.
Cast Megatron CONVERTED. Four mana for the Vehicle side is the whole point; the Tyrant side is where you flip TO after the damage, not where you start.

rows.name: Basilisk Collar
rows.text: find it before you find more ammunition. Without deathtouch you need a small creature to point at; with it, every shot dumps almost its full mana value into a player.
Convert in your postcombat main phase. The mana it adds scales with the life your opponents lost that turn, so a big cannon shot funds a second fatty the same turn.
